observations: A large face fills the frame, outlined in thick white and black lines, with two rectangular eye areas topped by spiky crown-like forms and a wide open mouth showing a row of white teeth.
Deep blue dominates the face and background, cut through by diagonal stripes of yellow, red, and teal in the forehead area, with stacked orange and red shapes along the right edge.

Small looping spirals appear at the left jaw, zigzag lines run along the top and bottom edges, and yellow cross-hatching fills the rectangular eye zones, adding a dense layered quality to the surface.
reading: The face pushes to every edge, leaving almost no neutral space. Two rectangular eye zones, each cross-hatched in yellow, sit beneath spiky forms that read as both decorative and aggressive. The wide-open mouth, teeth clearly countable, holds the composition open rather than closed. Blue dominates, but diagonal forehead stripes and stacked orange forms at the right edge keep the surface restless. The overall feeling is one of loud, unguarded exposure.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #273 and nnxyz nnotb #275, with title order and recorded creation order aligned here. Where #275 strips back to near-monochrome on yellow, #274 packs the surface with competing color bands.

connections.reason: Both works use toothed zigzag lines as a repeated mark and share red, yellow, and blue, but #273 spreads its forms loosely on a flat lavender ground while #274 compresses everything into a dense dark-blue face.

Both show a face with eye forms and a tooth-filled mouth, but #275 reduces the palette to white, grey, and yellow, making the contrast with #274's saturated blue-and-red surface direct and measurable.

lookingQuestion: The two rectangular eye zones share the same basic structure — what specific differences can you find between what fills the left and right eye areas?
ambiguities: The stacked orange and red shapes along the right edge are partially cropped; whether they form a separate figure or are background marks cannot be confirmed from this image alone.
The spiky forms above each eye could be read as crown shapes, eyelashes, or purely abstract marks; no supplied evidence resolves the intended reading.
